hints: Connect engine power, forward driving force, and speed using $P = F_D \times v$, converting $80\text{ kW}$ to $80000\text{ W}$ at speed $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
At constant speed up the incline, acceleration is zero, so the forward driving force balances all opposing forces along the slope.
Identify the two opposing forces acting down the hill: resistance ($850\text{ N}$) and the downslope component of weight ($mg\sin\theta = 1200 \times 10 \times \sin\theta = 12000\sin\theta$).
Set up $F_D = 850 + 12000\sin\theta$, substitute $F_D = \frac{80000}{24}$, and solve for $\theta$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the engine driving force $F_D$ moving up the hill at constant speed $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with power $P = 80\text{ kW} = 80000\text{ W}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{80000}{24} = \frac{10000}{3} \approx 3333.33\text{ N}$$

Since the car travels up the hill at constant speed, acceleration is zero, so the driving force balances both the resistance and the downslope component of weight:
$$F_D - 850 - mg\sin\theta = 0 \implies \frac{10000}{3} - 850 - 12000\sin\theta = 0$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the relationship connecting power, driving force, and velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v \implies F_D = \frac{P}{v}$$

Convert power $P = 80\text{ kW}$ to watts and substitute velocity $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{80000}{24} = \frac{10000}{3}\text{ N}$$

Analyze the forces acting parallel to the hill. Because the speed is constant, the net force along the slope is zero ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - F_{\text{res}} - mg\sin\theta = 0$$

Substitute the mass $m = 1200\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and resistance $F_{\text{res}} = 850\text{ N}$:
$$\frac{10000}{3} - 850 - 1200(10)\sin\theta = 0$$
$$\frac{10000}{3} - 850 - 12000\sin\theta = 0$$

Subtract $850$ from $\frac{10000}{3}$ by placing over a common denominator:
$$\frac{10000}{3} - \frac{2550}{3} = \frac{7450}{3}$$
$$\frac{7450}{3} = 12000\sin\theta$$

Divide both sides by $12000$ to isolate $\sin\theta$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{7450}{3 \times 12000} = \frac{7450}{36000} = \frac{149}{720} \approx 0.206944$$

Take the inverse sine to find the angle $\theta$:
$$\theta = \arcsin\left(\frac{149}{720}\right) \approx 11.944^\circ = 11.9^\circ \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
